correctness.rationale: The frozen and repaired proofs yield the exact signed rule: a border gives a period p<n whose missing closing edge is already inside the word (w_p=w_0), and a smaller period would force a longer border. With no border one takes the shortest positive directed return to the first symbol after the prescribed n−1 edges, including the case of a single letter. The k-border count is exactly tr(B^(n−k)), as the length-(n−k) prefix is a labeled closed walk with starting position fixed. PF word-count bounds provide a uniform tail for all k including overlapping borders. In the repair I checked the growing-block estimate explicitly: divide each bridge entry by its positive PF rank-one limit, giving a uniform relative error O_B(θ^(n−2s)) for s-block pairs after normalization. Summing against the product boundary probabilities preserves this bound in total variation. The two coherent boundary strings then give the signed limit after truncating at floor(n/3); a geometric tail times a polynomial controls the discarded moments on either law. In the example the endpoint event of terminal symbol one advance ahead has limiting probability 1/3; length one cannot match, all k≥2 match probabilities sum to 1/3, and a length-two constant match of mass 1/12 is disjoint from this endpoint event. Thus the residual union bound proves a positive negative atom, not an independence heuristic. Independent replay python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 3 compared periodic completions, the exact rule and trace counts for every word of lengths 1..8 in three primitive graphs, including one with no loops. The frozen checker was inspected, not run. The finite tests do not certify the limit.
